new_statements.translation: 2.10 As for the accent, as far as I could observe, there are only oxytone [final-stressed] and paroxytone [penult-stressed] words. Whether the accent was formerly intimately tied to tone (as that of Yaathe [Fulniô] still is today) cannot be proven; what is certain is that at present it is purely of a dynamic-expiratory nature. It seems that words are always oxytone when they end in: a) i, u; b) a nasal vowel; c) a diphthong; d) a consonant; e) a vowel preceded by y or j.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the final or the penultimate syllable, conditioned by the shape of the final syllable: final stress when the word ends in a consonant, a diphthong, a nasal vowel, a high vowel (i, u) or a vowel preceded by a glide (y/j); otherwise (words ending in a plain oral non-high vowel) penultimate stress is implied but not stated explicitly. Stress is dynamic (intensity), not tonal.
new_statements.exceptions: None listed; the rule is hedged ('pelo que pude observar', 'parece que sempre'); antepenultimate stress is said not to occur.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level. The data are isolated vocabulary items and a few Portuguese-matrix phrases collected in 1944 by Cícero Cavalcanti (SPI) from elderly rememberers at Cimbres/Serra do Ororubá after the language had ceased to be spoken (last fluent generation born 1860s-70s per Hohenthal 1954); Lapenda models the vowel system explicitly on Portuguese (§2.1), so the oxytone/paroxytone pattern may reflect Portuguese-speaking rememberers' pronunciation.
new_statements.identity_note: Lapenda 1962 describes the Xucuru of Cimbres / Serra do Ororubá (Pesqueira, PE) = xuku1239 proper, from rememberers' vocabulary (Cícero Cavalcanti's 1944 SPI collection). Not to be confused with Xukuru-Kariri of Palmeira dos Índios (Alagoas), which Meader 1978 lists separately (§3.10) and whose lists are largely Fulniô/Yaathe; Hohenthal 1954 warns that some 'Xucuru' items may be Paratió. The earlier scan classification (no source found, 'Lapenda 1962 is wordlist-level') is superseded: Lapenda 1962 is a short structural sketch with a phonology section (§§2.1-2.10) including an explicit stress statement.
